title: How the game was built
intro: In order, from the first public day. Each stamp is when that step landed (Atlantic, UTC−4). What was added or changed — not how it was built. There is still no public game download.

items.title: The 12 metre lane
changed: Dummy and rifle materials so the lane reads as a place, not a gray box

items.title: Lobby, settings, credit law
added: Score, time, and accuracy on the HUD
Credit only on a stopped head — walking heads do not count
changed: Each shot fires its own sound

items.title: Range stays on screen
changed: The lane no longer drops to a black screen

items.title: Menus and saved results
changed: Fast trigger taps register as separate shots

items.title: Kestrel and the hangar fill in
added: Original Kestrel in the hands — stock, mag, optic, rails
changed: Human targets no longer wear a real-world army identity

items.title: The website shows the range
changed: Site copy names an original lab, not another product

items.title: The hangar becomes a building
changed: 12 m head stays live in micro-correction

items.title: Impacts, dummy, and a quieter hangar
changed: Rifle combat HUD no longer shows always-on equip slots
Magazine dump and low-ready on the rifle

items.title: Hangar and impact rims
changed: Hangar even cleaner at the far end

items.title: Internal range build
added: A Windows range build for testers

items.title: Afterlight Volume One
added: Volume One on the site — 9,489 words

items.title: Afterlight radio
added: Seven shop-bench tracks on the site
Play, pause, shuffle, seek, volume knob

items.title: Character stills
changed: Gabriel, Camila, and the rest of the stills

items.title: AFTERLIGHT is the game on the site
added: Game, World, Training, Media, and Updates as their own pages
changed: Homepage leads with the Puerto Rico campaign, not only the range
